questions.title: Bench: zoomed in on all eight samples
Bench: dissolved salt until saturated; tried sand
Why is mineral water a mixture?
opts: Minerals are dissolved in it, and they are not chemically joined to the water.
Its water particles are made of hydrogen and oxygen atoms joined together.
It is a liquid, and every liquid that people drink is a mixture of substances.
It has only one phase, and a substance with only one phase is a mixture.

questions.title: Milk (extension)
opts: A mixture: fat droplets and proteins are spread through water, not joined to it.
A compound: fat, proteins and water are chemically joined into one substance.
A pure substance: it looks the same all through, so it has one kind of particle.
An element: it comes from one kind of animal, so it has one kind of atom.

questions.title: Bench: filtration of muddy water and salt water
Residue and filtrate in a coffee filter
Why did the salt pass through?
opts: The salt was dissolved, so its particles were small enough to pass through the holes.
The salt grains were heavier than the sand grains, so they fell straight through the paper.
The salt reacted with the paper and made the holes in the paper much bigger.
The water pushed the salt through because the funnel was filled too quickly.

questions.title: Which mixture can filtration separate?
opts: Chalk powder stirred into water
Sugar dissolved in warm tap water
Blue ink mixed with water
Salt dissolved in seawater

questions.title: Why does the water leave and the salt stay?
opts: Water is more volatile than salt: it turns into a gas at a much lower temperature.
Salt is more volatile than water: it turns into a gas first and then falls back down.
Salt is denser than water, so it sinks and stays in the basin while water rises.
Water particles are bigger than salt particles, so the heat pushes the water out.

questions.title: Why do crystals form as it cools?
opts: A cool solution can hold less dissolved solute, so the extra solute forms crystals.
A cool solution can hold more dissolved solute, so the solute joins into crystals.
Cooling makes the water react with the solute, and the new compound is a solid crystal.
Cooling makes the solvent boil away quickly, so only the crystals stay behind.

questions.title: Why does cold water go in at the bottom?
opts: So the jacket fills completely with cold water and cools all of the vapour.
So the cold water flows downhill and leaves the jacket as fast as it can.
So the vapour is pushed back into the flask and boils for a second time.
So the cold water mixes with the vapour and makes more distillate more quickly.

questions.title: The temperature while the distillate collects
Distillation or evaporation?
opts: In distillation the vapour is cooled and collected; in evaporation it is lost to the air.
In distillation the solid is collected; in evaporation the solid is lost to the air.
In distillation the liquid is never heated at all; in evaporation the liquid is always heated.
In distillation the solid dissolves again; in evaporation the solid forms crystals.

questions.title: When to change the beaker (extension)
opts: Change the beaker: the ethanol has gone, and water is about to collect.
Turn off the Bunsen: the mixture is now fully separated into two liquids.
Keep the same beaker: the ethanol and the water are collected together.
Add more ethanol: the flask needs it to keep the temperature at 78 °C.

questions.title: Bench: made the chromatogram of the five inks
Why a pencil start line?
opts: Pencil is insoluble in the solvent, so the line does not move or add colours.
Pencil is soluble in the solvent, so the line moves up the paper with the dyes.
Pencil lines are thicker than pen lines, so the ink spots are easier to see.
Pencil lines are darker than pen lines, so the dyes move further up the paper.

questions.title: Why the solvent stays below the line
opts: Otherwise the dyes dissolve into the water in the beaker instead of moving up.
Otherwise the water cannot reach the paper, and so the dyes do not move at all.
Otherwise the paper becomes too heavy, and it falls into the beaker of water.
Otherwise the lid cannot be closed, and the water evaporates from the beaker.

Stationary and mobile phase in a new method
Bench: separated oil and water with a separating funnel
Why is oil the top layer?
opts: Oil is less dense than water, so it floats on top of the water.
Oil is more dense than water, so it rises up above all the water.
Oil is more volatile than water, so it rises up to the top.
Oil is less soluble than water, so it stays above the water.

questions.title: Which pair can a separating funnel separate?
opts: Cooking oil and vinegar
Ethanol and water
Orange juice and water
Salt water and pure water

questions.title: Bench: sorted steel and aluminium cans with a magnet
Why do aluminium cans stay on the belt?
opts: Aluminium is not a magnetic metal, so the magnet does not attract it at all.
Aluminium cans are heavier than steel cans, so the magnet cannot lift them.
Aluminium is magnetic, but the paint on the cans stops the magnet attracting it.
Aluminium cans are empty, so there is no metal inside for the magnet to attract.

questions.title: Iron filings and sulfur
opts: Hold a magnet over the mixture: it attracts the iron filings.
Pour the mixture through filter paper: the iron stays on top.
Heat the mixture in a basin: the sulfur evaporates and leaves.
Stir the mixture into water: the iron filings float, and the sulfur sinks.
